card: PR 36042 raises the minimum supported GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1, verified at configure time by requiring C++20 std::format. This enables standard formatting and modern C++ template assertions while laying the groundwork for a transition to C++23. CI environments are updated to GCC 13 and Ubuntu 24.04, NetBSD cross-builds are removed from active GitHub Actions CI, and developers on older distributions lacking GCC 13 default packages will need Clang or alternative repositories.
changed_since_previous: Removed the ALWAYS_FALSE template helper in favor of direct static_assert(false), dropped explicit -Werror flags in native previous releases CI, and updated NetBSD cross-compile scripts to use libstdc++-14 packages.
evidence: The PR author notes in the description that "only C++20 std::format will become available, but this bump should also pave the way for C++23", pointing to discussion issue #34979 on dropping support for older host distributions.
problem: GCC 12 lacks standard library support for C++20 std::format and CWG2518 (relaxed static_assert in dependent contexts), requiring workarounds like tinyformat/ostringstream and custom types like ALWAYS_FALSE, while blocking progress toward C++23 adoption.

risk.why: A broken compiler check or unsupported compiler assumption could cause builds from source to fail for developers and packagers on older Linux distributions.

scope_notes: Combines build system and CI environment updates with compiler-feature usage (std::format in ToString and wallet benchmarks, removal of util/types.h ALWAYS_FALSE).
summary: Raises the minimum supported GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1 and validates C++20 std::format support during CMake configuration. It removes NetBSD cross-compilation from active GitHub Actions CI, updates the native previous releases CI image to Ubuntu 24.04 with GCC 13, and begins adopting std::format as well as standard static_assert(false) behavior.
